_comment: Managed-service dependencies of the fbctf application. These are NOT servers and are NOT discoverable by the AWS Transform discovery tool (no OS to reach via SSH/WinRM; the tool's database modules cover SQL Server and Oracle only, not MySQL). Captured here from the AWS control plane (describe-* APIs) and CloudWatch so a Transform assessment has the full dependency picture. Utilization window: 2026-08-27 ~16:00Z -> 22:37Z (boot + idle; not representative of a load test or a real event).

database.app_auth: application DB user created IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password (HHVM 3.21 client cannot speak caching_sha2_password)
database.estimated_dataset_note: FreeStorageSpace ~18.4 GiB of 20 GiB. Dataset is fbctf schema + seed data (countries.sql 146 KiB, logos.sql 23 KiB) plus scoreboard rows.

utilization.note: CPU + write-IOPS peaks are the one-time boot schema import. Steady state is near-zero.

consumed_by: i-0d6b944117ba6302b (app tier, HHVM - session store + config cache)

utilization.note: Effectively unused. ~54 KB of cache content, ~8 items. A db.t3.micro RDS handles this working set with no cache at all.

load_balancers.name: fbctf-demo-web
load_balancers.note: One target. No TLS. For a single-instance demo this is $16/mo of load balancer for one backend.

load_balancers.name: fbctf-demo-app
load_balancers.note: Exists only because FastCGI is not HTTP so an ALB cannot front HHVM (ADR 002). Disappears if nginx + HHVM run in one unit (container or single host).

nat_gateway.note: The 252 MB / 5-min peak is boot-time provisioning: apt, AWS CLI v2 (~60 MB), CloudWatch agent .deb, HHVM debs (31 MB), and the prebuilt app tarball (36.5 MB) from S3. S3 traffic traverses NAT at $0.045/GB because there is no S3 gateway VPC endpoint (which is free). Steady state is near-idle.

observability.alarm_actions: none (console-visible only; no SNS in demo scope)

artifacts_bucket.name: fbctf-demo-artifacts-337058058699-use1
artifacts_bucket.purpose: vendored packages + prebuilt app tarball; survives terraform destroy of the demo stack
